test_cases.description: AddRequirement with a non-duplicate ID returns a new RequirementsV1Json with the requirement appended and leaves the original unchanged.
preconditions: A RequirementsV1Json struct is constructed with one existing requirement having ID '05-REQ-1'
A new Requirement struct is constructed with ID '05-REQ-2'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: original := RequirementsV1Json{Requirements: [{id:'05-REQ-1'}]}; newReq, err := AddRequirement(original, Requirement{id:'05-REQ-2'}); assert err == nil; assert len(newReq.Requirements) == 2; assert newReq.Requirements[1].id == '05-REQ-2'; assert len(original.Requirements) == 1

test_cases.description: GetRequirement with an existing ID returns a pointer to the matching Requirement and true.
preconditions: A RequirementsV1Json struct is constructed with a requirement having ID '05-REQ-3'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: req := RequirementsV1Json{Requirements: [{id:'05-REQ-3', title:'Test Req'}]}; ptr, found := GetRequirement(req, '05-REQ-3'); assert found == true; assert ptr != nil; assert ptr.id == '05-REQ-3'

test_cases.description: GetRequirement with a non-existent ID returns nil and false.
preconditions: A RequirementsV1Json struct is constructed with a requirement having ID '05-REQ-1'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: req := RequirementsV1Json{Requirements: [{id:'05-REQ-1'}]}; ptr, found := GetRequirement(req, '05-REQ-99'); assert found == false; assert ptr == nil

test_cases.description: RemoveRequirement with an existing ID returns a new RequirementsV1Json without that requirement and true.
preconditions: A RequirementsV1Json struct is constructed with two requirements having IDs '05-REQ-1' and '05-REQ-2'
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: original := RequirementsV1Json{Requirements: [{id:'05-REQ-1'},{id:'05-REQ-2'}]}; newReq, ok := RemoveRequirement(original, '05-REQ-1'); assert ok == true; assert len(newReq.Requirements) == 1; assert newReq.Requirements[0].id == '05-REQ-2'; assert len(original.Requirements) == 2

test_cases.description: SetGlossaryEntry inserts a new term or overwrites an existing one and returns a new RequirementsV1Json without modifying the original.
preconditions: A RequirementsV1Json struct is constructed with an empty glossary map
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: original := RequirementsV1Json{Glossary: {}}; newReq := SetGlossaryEntry(original, 'Foo', 'A foo is a bar'); assert newReq.Glossary['Foo'] == 'A foo is a bar'; assert len(original.Glossary) == 0; newReq2 := SetGlossaryEntry(newReq, 'Foo', 'Updated definition'); assert newReq2.Glossary['Foo'] == 'Updated definition'

test_cases.description: RemoveGlossaryEntry with an existing term returns a new RequirementsV1Json without that term and true.
preconditions: A RequirementsV1Json struct is constructed with a glossary containing term 'Foo'

input.req: RequirementsV1Json with glossary={'Foo':'A foo is a bar'}

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: original := RequirementsV1Json{Glossary: {'Foo':'A foo is a bar'}}; newReq, ok := RemoveGlossaryEntry(original, 'Foo'); assert ok == true; assert 'Foo' not in newReq.Glossary; assert 'Foo' in original.Glossary

test_cases.description: DiscoverLintSpecs with a valid specsDir and empty filterSpec returns LintSpecInfo entries for all subdirectories containing requirements.json, with HasTasks and HasPRD set correctly.
preconditions: A temporary directory is created on the filesystem
Subdirectory '05-my_spec' is created containing requirements.json and tasks.json but no prd.md
Subdirectory '06-other_spec' is created containing requirements.json and prd.md but no tasks.json
Subdirectory 'not-a-spec' is created containing requirements.json (invalid name format)
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: specsDir := createTempDir(); createDir(specsDir+'/05-my_spec'); writeFile(specsDir+'/05-my_spec/requirements.json', '{}'); writeFile(specsDir+'/05-my_spec/tasks.json', '{}'); createDir(specsDir+'/06-other_spec'); writeFile(specsDir+'/06-other_spec/requirements.json', '{}'); writeFile(specsDir+'/06-other_spec/prd.md', ''); createDir(specsDir+'/not-a-spec'); writeFile(specsDir+'/not-a-spec/requirements.json', '{}'); infos, err := DiscoverLintSpecs(specsDir, ''); assert err == nil; assert len(infos) == 2; assert any(i.Name=='my_spec' && i.HasTasks==true && i.HasPRD==false for i in infos); assert any(i.Name=='other_spec' && i.HasTasks==false && i.HasPRD==true for i in infos)

test_cases.description: SortFindings returns a new slice sorted by SpecName ascending, then File ascending, then Severity in order error < warning < hint, without modifying the input.
preconditions: A slice of LintFinding values is constructed in an unsorted order

input.findings: [{SpecName:'b_spec', File:'a.json', Severity:'hint'}, {SpecName:'a_spec', File:'z.json', Severity:'warning'}, {SpecName:'a_spec', File:'a.json', Severity:'hint'}, {SpecName:'a_spec', File:'a.json', Severity:'error'}]

expected.sorted_order: [{SpecName:'a_spec', File:'a.json', Severity:'error'}, {SpecName:'a_spec', File:'a.json', Severity:'hint'}, {SpecName:'a_spec', File:'z.json', Severity:'warning'}, {SpecName:'b_spec', File:'a.json', Severity:'hint'}]

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: input := [{SpecName:'b_spec',File:'a.json',Severity:'hint'},{SpecName:'a_spec',File:'z.json',Severity:'warning'},{SpecName:'a_spec',File:'a.json',Severity:'hint'},{SpecName:'a_spec',File:'a.json',Severity:'error'}]; inputCopy := copy(input); sorted := SortFindings(input); assert sorted[0] == {SpecName:'a_spec',File:'a.json',Severity:'error'}; assert sorted[1] == {SpecName:'a_spec',File:'a.json',Severity:'hint'}; assert sorted[2] == {SpecName:'a_spec',File:'z.json',Severity:'warning'}; assert sorted[3] == {SpecName:'b_spec',File:'a.json',Severity:'hint'}; assert input == inputCopy

test_cases.description: ComputeExitCode returns 1 when at least one finding has Severity 'error'.
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: findings := [{Severity:'warning'},{Severity:'error'},{Severity:'hint'}]; code := ComputeExitCode(findings); assert code == 1

test_cases.description: ComputeExitCode returns 0 when no finding has Severity 'error'.
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: findings := [{Severity:'warning'},{Severity:'hint'}]; code := ComputeExitCode(findings); assert code == 0

test_cases.description: RunLintSpecs with lintAll=true discovers all specs, validates each, collects findings, sorts them, computes exit code, and returns a LintResult.
preconditions: A temporary specs directory is created on the filesystem
Two spec subdirectories are created, each containing a valid requirements.json
One spec has a validation error (e.g. missing required field)
test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: specsDir := createTempSpecsDir(); result, err := RunLintSpecs(specsDir, true); assert err == nil; assert result.ExitCode == 0 or 1; assert result.Findings is sorted by SortFindings criteria; assert result.ExitCode == ComputeExitCode(result.Findings)

test_cases.description: RunLintSpecs with lintAll=false skips specs where all subtasks are in state 'done' or 'dropped' and excludes them from findings.
preconditions: A temporary specs directory is created on the filesystem
Spec '05-my_spec' has requirements.json and tasks.json where all subtasks have state 'done'

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: specsDir := createTempSpecsDir(); result, err := RunLintSpecs(specsDir, false); assert err == nil; assert none(f.SpecName == 'my_spec' for f in result.Findings); assert any(f.SpecName == 'other_spec' for f in result.Findings) or result.Findings is empty for other_spec if it has no issues

test_cases.description: RunLintSpecs with lintAll=false includes specs that have no tasks.json or have at least one subtask not in 'done' or 'dropped' state.
preconditions: A temporary specs directory is created on the filesystem
Spec '05-no_tasks' has requirements.json but no tasks.json

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: specsDir := createTempSpecsDir(); result, err := RunLintSpecs(specsDir, false); assert err == nil; specsLinted := unique(f.SpecName for f in result.Findings); assert 'no_tasks' in specsLinted or no_tasks spec was linted (even if no findings); assert 'in_progress' in specsLinted or in_progress spec was linted

test_cases.description: Any Next*ID function called on an empty collection returns the ID with numeric suffix 1.

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: emptyReq := RequirementsV1Json{SpecID:'05'}; emptyTs := TestSpecV1Json{SpecID:'05'}; emptyR := Requirement{id:'05-REQ-1'}; assert NextRequirementID(emptyReq) == '05-REQ-1'; assert NextCriterionID(emptyR) == '05-REQ-1.1'; assert NextEdgeCaseID(emptyR) == '05-REQ-1.E1'; assert NextCorrectnessPropertyID(emptyReq) == '05-PROP-1'; assert NextExecutionPathID(emptyReq) == '05-PATH-1'; assert NextErrorHandlingID(emptyReq) == '05-ERR-1'; assert NextTestCaseID(emptyTs) == 'TS-05-1'; assert NextPropertyTestID(emptyTs) == 'TS-05-P1'; assert NextEdgeCaseTestID(emptyTs) == 'TS-05-E1'; assert NextSmokeTestID(emptyTs) == 'TS-05-SMOKE-1'

property_tests.description: For any mutation function, the input struct is byte-for-byte identical after the call returns, regardless of success or error.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random RequirementsV1Json structs with 0-10 requirements, 0-5 glossary entries, and 0-5 correctness properties. For each, generate a random Requirement to add (sometimes with a duplicate ID to trigger the error path). Serialize the input struct to JSON before and after the call.
property_tests.invariant_check: serialized_before := json.Marshal(input); call mutation function; serialized_after := json.Marshal(input); assert serialized_before == serialized_after

property_tests.description: Any Add* mutation function called twice with items sharing the same ID always returns a non-nil error on the second call and the returned collection is identical to the input.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random valid IDs and random collection structs. Call each Add* function once to add an item, then call it again with the same item ID. Sample all Add* functions: AddRequirement, AddCriterion, AddEdgeCase, AddTestCase, AddPropertyTest, AddEdgeCaseTest, AddSmokeTest, AddTaskGroup, AddSubtask, AddTraceabilityEntry.
property_tests.invariant_check: result1, err1 := AddX(collection, item); assert err1 == nil; result2, err2 := AddX(result1, item); assert err2 != nil; assert json.Marshal(result2) == json.Marshal(result1)

property_tests.description: For any Next*ID function, calling it, adding an item with the returned ID, then calling it again yields a strictly greater numeric suffix.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random RequirementsV1Json structs with 0-20 requirements using IDs with random numeric suffixes (including non-contiguous sequences). Repeat for TestSpecV1Json and Requirement. Run 50 iterations per entity type.
property_tests.invariant_check: id1 := NextRequirementID(collection); newCollection, _ := AddRequirement(collection, Requirement{id:id1}); id2 := NextRequirementID(newCollection); suffix1 := extractNumericSuffix(id1); suffix2 := extractNumericSuffix(id2); assert suffix2 > suffix1

property_tests.description: Any Next*ID function called on an empty collection always returns an ID with numeric suffix 1.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: For each Next*ID function, construct an empty collection with a randomly chosen spec_id string (e.g. '01' through '99'). Run 20 iterations per function.
property_tests.invariant_check: id := NextRequirementID(emptyCollection); suffix := extractNumericSuffix(id); assert suffix == 1; // repeat for all Next*ID functions

property_tests.description: SortFindings returns the same result regardless of the input ordering.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random slices of 0-20 LintFinding values with random SpecName, File, and Severity fields (from the set 'error', 'warning', 'hint'). Generate all permutations for small slices (<=6 elements) and 100 random shuffles for larger slices.
property_tests.invariant_check: sorted1 := SortFindings(permutation1); sorted2 := SortFindings(permutation2); assert sorted1 == sorted2 for all permutations of the same input set

property_tests.description: ComputeExitCode returns 1 if and only if at least one finding has Severity 'error', and 0 otherwise.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random slices of 0-50 LintFinding values with Severity randomly chosen from 'error', 'warning', 'hint'. Also generate slices with no 'error' findings and slices with all 'error' findings. Run 100 iterations.
property_tests.invariant_check: hasError := any(f.Severity == 'error' for f in findings); code := ComputeExitCode(findings); assert (code == 1) == hasError

property_tests.description: LoadDependentInterfaces never returns an error and never panics for any input, always returning a slice (possibly empty).
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random specID strings ('01' through '99') and random specRoot paths (valid directories, non-existent paths, empty directories, directories with malformed spec folders). Run 30 iterations covering all error scenarios.
property_tests.invariant_check: result := LoadDependentInterfaces(specID, specRoot); assert result != nil; // function signature returns []map[string]any not ([]map[string]any, error) so no error to check; assert no panic occurred

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test for programmatic requirement addition: NextRequirementID generates a valid ID, AddRequirement appends the requirement to a new copy, and the result can be serialized to requirements.json.
smoke_tests.trigger: Call NextRequirementID on a RequirementsV1Json with existing requirements, construct a Requirement with the returned ID, call AddRequirement, and serialize the result.
expected_effects: NextRequirementID returns a string matching the pattern '{spec_id}-REQ-{N}' where N is max existing suffix + 1
AddRequirement returns (RequirementsV1Json, nil) with the new requirement appended
The original RequirementsV1Json is not modified
The returned RequirementsV1Json can be marshaled to valid JSON without error
The marshaled JSON contains the new requirement ID

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test for the spec lint CLI command execution path: RunLintSpecs discovers specs, loads and validates each, collects findings, sorts them, and returns a LintResult with correct exit code.
smoke_tests.trigger: Create a temporary specs directory with at least two spec subdirectories (one with a validation issue, one clean), then call RunLintSpecs with lintAll=true.
real_components: afspec lint package (RunLintSpecs, DiscoverLintSpecs, SortFindings, ComputeExitCode)
mockable: filesystem (temporary spec directories and requirements.json files)
expected_effects: DiscoverLintSpecs returns LintSpecInfo entries for all subdirectories containing requirements.json
LoadSpec is called for each discovered spec
Validate is called on each loaded Spec
ValidationResult entries are converted to LintFinding structs
SortFindings returns findings in deterministic order (SpecName asc, File asc, Severity error < warning < hint)
ComputeExitCode returns 1 if any finding has Severity 'error', else 0
RunLintSpecs returns (LintResult, nil) with Findings and ExitCode populated

smoke_tests.description: End-to-end smoke test for cross-spec interface loading: LoadDependentInterfaces discovers specs, builds the dependency graph, loads upstream specs, and returns interface maps.
smoke_tests.trigger: Create a temporary specRoot with two spec directories where spec '05' depends on spec '04', then call LoadDependentInterfaces('05', specRoot).
mockable: filesystem (temporary spec directories with requirements.json files)
expected_effects: DiscoverSpecs returns SpecMeta entries for all specs under specRoot
BuildDependencyGraph resolves upstream dependencies for spec '05'
LoadSpec is called for each upstream dependency
Glossary entries, external API symbols, and criterion return contracts are extracted into map[string]any per upstream spec
LoadDependentInterfaces returns a non-nil slice with one entry per successfully loaded upstream spec
If any step fails, LoadDependentInterfaces returns an empty slice without panicking or returning an error
